messages:
emma_chu: Hi team — quick help? I have a last-minute pediatric dentist appt for my 5mo tomorrow. Dentist is asking for member ID or proof of coverage. I don't have my physical card on me. Plan = Redwood Standard PPO. Any quick way to get a temporary ID or check if this dentist is in-network? Thanks!

mike_peopleops: Hey Emma — we can help. Quick options:
1) Digital ID: log into the Redwood Benefits Portal (https://benefits.redwood.example) -> My Benefits -> ID Cards -> Download temporary ID (PDF). Works for both primary + dependents.
2) Provider lookup: use the insurer's search via that portal (Benefits Portal -> Find Care) or call the insurer's provider line listed on the portal.
3) If the provider is out-of-network, they can submit a claim — keep the itemized receipt and CPT codes.

If you want, DM me your dependent's DOB and the dentist name and I'll check network status.

benefits_bot: Automated message: A temporary ID PDF has been emailed to emma_chu@redwood.com and is available at the portal. (Masking applied for security) :email:

emma_chu: Got the PDF, thanks! One follow-up — if they say 'we're not in-network' and ask for estimated copay, what do I tell them for this plan?

nia_hr: For Redwood Standard PPO, basic pediatric dentistry (routine exam/cleaning) typically has $0 copay in-network for dependents under 18; out-of-network will be subject to allowed amount and coinsurance — provider may balance bill. Best to have them estimate charges and give you an itemized receipt so you can submit for reimbursement. Typical timeline: allow up to 90 days for reimbursement processing.

mike_peopleops: Also: if they need a quick pre-auth, request a predetermination from the insurer before the procedure — use the pre-auth form on the portal and upload the x-rays/procedure plan. If you want, I can kick that off with the insurer team this afternoon. :thumbsup:

emma_chu: Appreciate it — please kick it off if you can. DMing dentist name now. Thanks all :heart:
